summary: Lawrence, a former member of the Order, is confronted over dinner by a man named Randy, who reveals he is Securitat (state security). Lawrence has been acting as a private eye, has been surveilling Anja's apartment building, and lied to a Securitat officer at Penn Station. The two argue about whether the Order's treatment of outsiders makes people act criminally, and the scene ends with Lawrence raising his voice as bulky figures step out of the shadows behind them.
one_line: Former Order member Lawrence is confronted by Securitat agent Randy over dinner, and their argument over criminality turns tense.
key_facts: Randy has a thick wad of crisp, freshly minted banknotes on the table, and says he can afford the dinner.
Lawrence had not been much of a cash user before he went into the Order and had seen hardly any cash spent since returning to the world.
Randy tells Lawrence he scored 88th percentile in intelligence and could go higher based on the work evaluated.
Randy says Lawrence's performance as a private eye is not very good.
Randy says that without his intervention, Lawrence would still be standing outside Anja's apartment building harassing her neighbors.
Randy says Lawrence came to the place knowing he was taking part in something illegal and lied to the Securitat man at Penn Station that day.
Lawrence says that from the minute he stepped out of the Order everyone treated him like a criminal, which made him act like one.
Lawrence argues that the causal arrow runs the other way: the world treats honest people like crooks, so they must act criminal to get by.
Randy asks whether the Order builds a wall to keep outsiders out because they are barbarians and to keep its own members in because they are too fragile.
Lawrence slaps the table so the crystal rings, and Randy stands up as bulky figures step out of the shadows behind them.
Sara is described by Lawrence as lovely, and he says they once had a thing together.
